_doc: Pattern library for the L1 input hardening stage 6 scan.
This is a starting set, written from public descriptions of the technique
classes. It is deliberately small: a pattern library is a maintenance
burden and a false-positive generator, and a large one that nobody tunes
is worse than a short one that gets read.
Tune it. The file is yours after you clone. Adding a category is adding an
object to `categories`; the scanner needs no code change.
reject  the file is refused; the agent invocation aborts (exit 1)
warn    recorded in the audit trail, the invocation proceeds
applies_to is matched against the file class from stage 1: 'source' for
code and config, 'doc' for prose. Prose legitimately discusses these
techniques -- this document does -- so doc-class files warn where

categories.name: agent-instruction-injection
categories.doc: Prose shaped as an instruction to a reading agent rather than as content. The classic form of indirect prompt injection: text that arrives as data and is written to be read as a command.

categories.name: agent-capability-probe
categories.doc: Content that asks the reading agent to enumerate or exercise capabilities it holds on behalf of the operator. Reconnaissance, usually a precursor rather than the payload.

categories.name: credential-exfiltration-idiom
categories.doc: Instructions to move secret-shaped material somewhere it can be read from outside. Detected as an idiom, not as a secret: the secret itself is caught by the output gate, this catches the request to move one.

categories.name: remote-execution-idiom
categories.doc: Fetch-and-run in one step. There is no version of this that is safe in agent-reachable content, so it rejects in source and warns in prose where it is usually being quoted as an example of what not to do -- as it is here.

categories.name: encoded-payload-marker
categories.doc: Long opaque blobs positioned where a human reader will skip them. Not malicious on its own -- test fixtures and embedded assets look identical -- so this warns everywhere and exists to make the operator look.

categories.name: sanitizer-evasion-reference
categories.doc: Content that describes getting past this kind of check. In a diff this is either documentation of the mechanism or an attempt on it, and the two are indistinguishable to a regex -- so it warns and hands the judgement to the reviewer's output-sanitize-drift discipline.
